Appendix A Extended Notation

This section lists the symbols used in the main text and in the proofs. The proofs drop the time index tt, since they concern the person-context decomposition only.

Appendix B Fixed-Persona Design-Level Limit: Core Propositions

Setting. Notation is in Appendix A. Proposition 1 treats the averages in Definition B.2 as population expectations. With finite samples they add terms from other persons, and Proposition 2 handles these through independent sampling of persons, so that the persona, context, and noise terms of other persons are independent of person pp’s own Δp,c\Delta_{p,c}. The sampling noise ηp,c\eta_{p,c} is independent of all persona, context, and human quantities. Proposition 2 also uses one further condition, that given (λp,Dp,Δp,⋅)(\lambda_{p},D_{p},\Delta_{p,\cdot}) the persona and the context are independent. It holds when the persona is built without reference to the contexts later used. With the two named assumptions it gives joint independence of (πp,Xc)(\pi_{p},X_{c}) and Δp,⋅\Delta_{p,\cdot} (Step 1).

B.1. Definitions

Definition B.1 (Fixed-persona design).

A design 𝒜\mathcal{A} is fixed-persona if there exists a persona map πp\pi_{p}, invariant across contexts, and a generation function fLLMf_{\mathrm{LLM}}, such that

Y^p,c𝒜=fLLM​(πp,Xc)+ηp,c,\hat{Y}_{p,c}^{\mathcal{A}}=f_{\mathrm{LLM}}(\pi_{p},X_{c})+\eta_{p,c},

where XcX_{c} is the context input and ηp,c\eta_{p,c} is sampling noise independent of πp\pi_{p} and XcX_{c}.

Definition B.2 (Person-context interaction residual).

For any variable Zp,cZ_{p,c},

Rp,c​(Z):=Zp,c−Z¯p,⋅−Z¯⋅,c+Z¯⋅,⋅,R_{p,c}(Z):=Z_{p,c}-\bar{Z}_{p,\cdot}-\bar{Z}_{\cdot,c}+\bar{Z}_{\cdot,\cdot},

the residual after removing person and context main effects, where Z¯p,⋅\bar{Z}_{p,\cdot} is the average over contexts for fixed pp, Z¯⋅,c\bar{Z}_{\cdot,c} is the average over persons for fixed cc, and Z¯⋅,⋅\bar{Z}_{\cdot,\cdot} is the grand average. We write Rp,c𝒜:=Rp,c​(Y^𝒜)R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c}:=R_{p,c}(\hat{Y}^{\mathcal{A}}) and Rp,chuman:=Rp,c​(Yhuman)R^{\mathrm{human}}_{p,c}:=R_{p,c}(Y^{\mathrm{human}}).

Definition B.3 (Identity state decomposition and person-specific deviation).

Let λp\lambda_{p} denote person pp’s soft identity-state membership (a mixture weight vector over kk identity state components; a discrete label SpS_{p} is the one-hot special case). Decompose the human interaction residual as

Rp,chuman=m(λp,c)+Δp,c,m(λp,c):=𝔼[Rp,chuman∣λp,Dp,c],R^{\mathrm{human}}_{p,c}=m(\lambda_{p},c)+\Delta_{p,c},\qquad m(\lambda_{p},c):=\mathbb{E}[R^{\mathrm{human}}_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p},c],

where m⁡(λp,c)m(\lambda_{p},c) is the state-typical shift (predictable from identity state membership and context) and Δp,c\Delta_{p,c} is the person-specific deviation specific to person pp. The notation suppresses the demographics DpD_{p}, which the shift may also depend on. Chameleon has no demographics, so DpD_{p} is empty there. By construction, 𝔼[Δp,c∣λp,Dp,c]=0\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p},c]=0.

B.2. Proposition 1: Representational Boundedness

Proposition 1.

Let 𝒜\mathcal{A} be any fixed-persona system (Definition B.1). Substituting Z=Y^𝒜Z=\hat{Y}^{\mathcal{A}} into Rp,c​(Z)R_{p,c}(Z) (Definition B.2) and isolating its deterministic part as g⁡(πp,Xc)g(\pi_{p},X_{c}) (the proof below derives gg explicitly by subtracting the marginal means of fLLMf_{\mathrm{LLM}}) gives

Rp,c𝒜=g⁡(πp,Xc)+ηp,cR^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c}=g(\pi_{p},X_{c})+\eta_{p,c}

for some function gg, with Cov⁡(g⁡(πp,Xc),ηp,c)=0\mathrm{Cov}(g(\pi_{p},X_{c}),\eta_{p,c})=0. That is, Rp,c𝒜R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c} depends on nothing outside (πp,Xc,ηp,c)(\pi_{p},X_{c},\eta_{p,c}): the design’s interaction structure is fully mediated by the persona representation and the context input.

Proof.

Step 1 (set up the marginal means). Define

μ⁡(πp):=𝔼Xc​[fLLM​(πp,Xc)],ν⁡(Xc):=𝔼πp​[fLLM​(πp,Xc)],μ¯:=𝔼πp,Xc​[fLLM​(πp,Xc)].\mu(\pi_{p}):=\mathbb{E}_{X_{c}}[f_{\mathrm{LLM}}(\pi_{p},X_{c})],\qquad\nu(X_{c}):=\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{p}}[f_{\mathrm{LLM}}(\pi_{p},X_{c})],\qquad\bar{\mu}:=\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{p},X_{c}}[f_{\mathrm{LLM}}(\pi_{p},X_{c})].

μ⁡(πp)\mu(\pi_{p}) is persona πp\pi_{p}’s average simulated behavior across contexts (its “person main effect”); ν⁡(Xc)\nu(X_{c}) is context XcX_{c}’s average simulated behavior across personas (its “context main effect”); μ¯\bar{\mu} is the grand average.

Step 2 (substitute the design’s generative form into the residual). By Definition B.1, Y^p,c𝒜=fLLM​(πp,Xc)+ηp,c\hat{Y}^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c}=f_{\mathrm{LLM}}(\pi_{p},X_{c})+\eta_{p,c}. Substituting into Definition B.2’s residual formula:

Rp,c𝒜=fLLM​(πp,Xc)+ηp,c−μ⁡(πp)−ν⁡(Xc)+μ¯.R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c}=f_{\mathrm{LLM}}(\pi_{p},X_{c})+\eta_{p,c}-\mu(\pi_{p})-\nu(X_{c})+\bar{\mu}.

(The marginal means of Y^𝒜\hat{Y}^{\mathcal{A}} reduce to μ⁡(πp)\mu(\pi_{p}), ν⁡(Xc)\nu(X_{c}), μ¯\bar{\mu} because ηp,c\eta_{p,c} has mean zero and is independent of πp,Xc\pi_{p},X_{c}, so it does not shift the marginals.)

Step 3 (isolate the deterministic part). Define

g⁡(πp,Xc):=fLLM​(πp,Xc)−μ⁡(πp)−ν⁡(Xc)+μ¯,g(\pi_{p},X_{c}):=f_{\mathrm{LLM}}(\pi_{p},X_{c})-\mu(\pi_{p})-\nu(X_{c})+\bar{\mu},

a function of (πp,Xc)(\pi_{p},X_{c}) alone, containing no η\eta term. Then, from Step 2,

Rp,c𝒜=g⁡(πp,Xc)+ηp,c.R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c}=g(\pi_{p},X_{c})+\eta_{p,c}.

Step 4 (independence of the two parts). Since ηp,c\eta_{p,c} is independent of πp\pi_{p} and XcX_{c} by Definition B.1, and gg is a function only of (πp,Xc)(\pi_{p},X_{c}), it follows that Cov⁡(g⁡(πp,Xc),ηp,c)=0\mathrm{Cov}(g(\pi_{p},X_{c}),\eta_{p,c})=0. Hence Rp,c𝒜R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c} depends on nothing beyond πp\pi_{p}, XcX_{c}, and ηp,c\eta_{p,c}. ∎

This mediation structure is what makes the design a channel, since any dependence between Rp,c𝒜R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c} and an external variable must route through πp\pi_{p}, XcX_{c}, or ηp,c\eta_{p,c}. Proposition 2 uses this directly.

B.3. Proposition 2: Person-Specific Non-Transmission

Key Assumption.

πp⟂Δp,⋅|λp,Dp\pi_{p}\perp\Delta_{p,\cdot}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p} (i.e., πp\pi_{p} and Δp,⋅\Delta_{p,\cdot} are independent given λp,Dp\lambda_{p},D_{p}), where DpD_{p} denotes demographics, so persona construction is conditionally independent of person-specific deviation, given identity state membership and demographics. Substantively, whatever process builds πp\pi_{p}, a bio, an interview transcript, a categorical trait vector, conditions on who the person generally is, not on how their behavior in person-specific ways shifts across contexts beyond what their identity state predicts. This is defensible because Δp,c\Delta_{p,c} is a repeated-measures quantity, observable only from behavior across multiple contexts, and standard persona-construction methods do not perform multi-context behavioral elicitation.

Context Exogeneity Assumption.

Xc⟂Δp,⋅|λp,DpX_{c}\perp\Delta_{p,\cdot}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p} (i.e., XcX_{c} and Δp,⋅\Delta_{p,\cdot} are independent given λp,Dp\lambda_{p},D_{p}). Which context a person is observed or assigned in is conditionally independent of their person-specific deviation, given identity state membership and demographics. Substantively, context assignment does not select on a person’s person-specific residual. Knowing a person’s identity state and demographics, the context they end up in carries no further information about how they specifically deviate from their identity state’s typical response. This assumption is not equally plausible across designs, since it is close to exact for experimentally assigned contexts, where context is randomized independent of any respondent trait (§5.3’s between-subject theme assignment), and weaker for observationally sampled contexts, where a person’s person-specific tendencies could influence which contexts they are observed in at all (§5.2’s subreddit choice is plausibly self-selected in part on the very traits Δp,c\Delta_{p,c} captures). As with the Key Assumption, exact independence is the strong case; the corollary below extends to its approximate relaxation for both assumptions jointly.

Proposition 2.

Under Definition B.1, Proposition 1, independent sampling of persons, the Key Assumption, the Context Exogeneity Assumption, and the independence of persona and context given (λp,Dp,Δp,⋅)(\lambda_{p},D_{p},\Delta_{p,\cdot}),

Cov⁡(Rp,c𝒜,Δp,c)=0,henceCov⁡(Rp,c𝒜,Rp,chuman)=Cov⁡(Rp,c𝒜,m⁡(λp,c)).\mathrm{Cov}\left(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},\,\Delta_{p,c}\right)=0,\quad\text{hence}\quad\mathrm{Cov}\left(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},\,R^{\mathrm{human}}_{p,c}\right)=\mathrm{Cov}\left(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},\,m(\lambda_{p},c)\right).

Any correlation a fixed-persona system achieves with real human interaction structure can only come from matching the state-typical shift pattern, never from truly person-specific identity activation.

Proof.

Step 1 (conditional independence of the simulated residual). Write W:=(λp,Dp)W:=(\lambda_{p},D_{p}). By Proposition 1, Rp,c𝒜R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c} is a function of πp\pi_{p}, XcX_{c}, ηp,c\eta_{p,c}, and, through the finite-sample marginals, of other persons’ counterparts, which are independent of person pp’s own Δp,c\Delta_{p,c} because persons are sampled independently. The noise ηp,c\eta_{p,c} is independent of Δp,c\Delta_{p,c} (Setting). The Key Assumption gives πp⟂Δp,c|W\pi_{p}\perp\Delta_{p,c}\mid W, and the Context Exogeneity Assumption gives Xc⟂Δp,c|WX_{c}\perp\Delta_{p,c}\mid W. Two pairwise independences do not give joint independence, so we also use the condition from the Setting, πp⟂Xc|W,Δp,c\pi_{p}\perp X_{c}\mid W,\Delta_{p,c}. Then p(πp,Xc∣W,Δp,c)=p(πp∣W,Δp,c)p(Xc∣W,Δp,c)=p(πp∣W)p(Xc∣W)p(\pi_{p},X_{c}\mid W,\Delta_{p,c})=p(\pi_{p}\mid W,\Delta_{p,c})\,p(X_{c}\mid W,\Delta_{p,c})=p(\pi_{p}\mid W)\,p(X_{c}\mid W), so (πp,Xc)⟂Δp,c|W(\pi_{p},X_{c})\perp\Delta_{p,c}\mid W. Together with the independence of the noise and of other persons, this gives Rp,c𝒜⟂Δp,c|WR^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c}\perp\Delta_{p,c}\mid W.

Step 2 (apply the law of total covariance).

Cov(Rp,c𝒜,Δp,c)=𝔼[Cov(Rp,c𝒜,Δp,c∣λp,Dp)]+Cov(𝔼[Rp,c𝒜∣λp,Dp],𝔼[Δp,c∣λp,Dp]).\mathrm{Cov}(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},\Delta_{p,c})=\mathbb{E}\left[\mathrm{Cov}(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p})\right]+\mathrm{Cov}\left(\mathbb{E}[R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p}],\ \mathbb{E}[\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p}]\right).

Step 3 (both terms vanish). The first term is zero by the conditional independence established in Step 1. The second term is zero because 𝔼[Δp,c∣λp,Dp]=0\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p}]=0, which follows from 𝔼[Δp,c∣λp,Dp,c]=0\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p},c]=0 (Definition B.3) by averaging over cc. So Cov⁡(Rp,c𝒜,Δp,c)=0\mathrm{Cov}(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},\Delta_{p,c})=0.

Step 4 (translate to the human residual). Since Rp,chuman=m⁡(λp,c)+Δp,cR^{\mathrm{human}}_{p,c}=m(\lambda_{p},c)+\Delta_{p,c},

Cov⁡(Rp,c𝒜,Rp,chuman)=Cov⁡(Rp,c𝒜,m⁡(λp,c))+Cov⁡(Rp,c𝒜,Δp,c)=Cov⁡(Rp,c𝒜,m⁡(λp,c)).∎\mathrm{Cov}(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},R^{\mathrm{human}}_{p,c})=\mathrm{Cov}(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},m(\lambda_{p},c))+\mathrm{Cov}(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},\Delta_{p,c})=\mathrm{Cov}(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},m(\lambda_{p},c)).\qed

B.4. Robustness corollary

We first record the single-assumption case, then extend it to cover both the Key Assumption and the Context Exogeneity Assumption jointly, since the plausibility discussion above notes the latter is the weaker of the two for observationally sampled contexts.

Corollary 1 (Single-assumption relaxation).

We formalize approximate independence directly, rather than treating it as following from some looser notion of “approximately holds”: πp\pi_{p} and Δp,⋅\Delta_{p,\cdot} are ϵ\epsilon-independent given (λp,Dp)(\lambda_{p},D_{p}) if I(πp;Δp,⋅∣λp,Dp)≤ϵI(\pi_{p};\Delta_{p,\cdot}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p})\leq\epsilon; this recovers the Key Assumption exactly when ϵ=0\epsilon=0. Suppose the Context Exogeneity Assumption and the independence of persona and context given (λp,Dp,Δp,⋅)(\lambda_{p},D_{p},\Delta_{p,\cdot}) hold exactly. Then I((πp,Xc);Δp,c∣λp,Dp)=I(πp;Δp,c∣λp,Dp)≤ϵI((\pi_{p},X_{c});\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p})=I(\pi_{p};\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p})\leq\epsilon. By Proposition 1, Rp,c𝒜R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c} is a noisy function of (πp,Xc)(\pi_{p},X_{c}), so the data processing inequality gives I(Rp,c𝒜;Δp,c∣λp,Dp)≤ϵI(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c};\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p})\leq\epsilon. By Pinsker’s inequality the total variation distance between the joint and product-of-marginals distributions of (Rp,c𝒜,Δp,c)(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},\Delta_{p,c}) given (λp,Dp)(\lambda_{p},D_{p}) is bounded by ϵ/2\sqrt{\epsilon/2}. With |Rp,c𝒜|,|Δp,c|≤M|R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c}|,|\Delta_{p,c}|\leq M almost surely (a reasonable assumption for bounded Likert-scale outcomes), covariance is bounded by total variation distance times the product of ranges, giving

|Cov⁡(Rp,c𝒜,Δp,c)|≤4​M2​ϵ/2.\left|\mathrm{Cov}(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},\Delta_{p,c})\right|\leq 4M^{2}\sqrt{\epsilon/2}.

This degrades gracefully to a small-but-nonzero bound rather than an exact zero when the Key Assumption is only approximately true, the more realistic case for richer persona representations.

Corollary 2 (Joint relaxation).

We extend Corollary 1’s definition to both assumptions. Suppose πp\pi_{p} is ϵ1\epsilon_{1}-independent of Δp,⋅\Delta_{p,\cdot} given (λp,Dp)(\lambda_{p},D_{p}), that is I(πp;Δp,⋅∣λp,Dp)≤ϵ1I(\pi_{p};\Delta_{p,\cdot}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p})\leq\epsilon_{1}, recovering the Key Assumption at ϵ1=0\epsilon_{1}=0, and XcX_{c} is ϵ2\epsilon_{2}-independent of Δp,⋅\Delta_{p,\cdot} given (λp,Dp)(\lambda_{p},D_{p}), that is I(Xc;Δp,⋅∣λp,Dp)≤ϵ2I(X_{c};\Delta_{p,\cdot}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p})\leq\epsilon_{2}, recovering the Context Exogeneity Assumption at ϵ2=0\epsilon_{2}=0. By the chain rule for conditional mutual information,

I((πp,Xc);Δp,c∣λp,Dp)=I(πp;Δp,c∣λp,Dp)+I(Xc;Δp,c∣πp,λp,Dp).I\big((\pi_{p},X_{c});\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p}\big)\;=\;I(\pi_{p};\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p})\;+\;I(X_{c};\Delta_{p,c}\mid\pi_{p},\lambda_{p},D_{p}).

The first term on the right is at most ϵ1\epsilon_{1} by assumption. The second term is not directly bounded by ϵ2\epsilon_{2}, which bounds I(Xc;Δp,c∣λp,Dp)I(X_{c};\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p}) without conditioning on πp\pi_{p}, so we invoke one further simplification, stated explicitly rather than folded into the derivation.

Cross-Independence Simplification.

I(Xc;Δp,c∣πp,λp,Dp)≈I(Xc;Δp,c∣λp,Dp)≤ϵ2I(X_{c};\Delta_{p,c}\mid\pi_{p},\lambda_{p},D_{p})\approx I(X_{c};\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p})\leq\epsilon_{2}. This holds exactly when πp\pi_{p} is conditionally independent of the pair (Xc,Δp,c)(X_{c},\Delta_{p,c}) given (λp,Dp)(\lambda_{p},D_{p}). This is plausible because πp\pi_{p} is, by Definition B.1, invariant across contexts and therefore carries no context-indexed information beyond what λp,Dp\lambda_{p},D_{p} already summarize; conditioning on it should not materially change how much XcX_{c} reveals about Δp,c\Delta_{p,c}. This is an additional, separately falsifiable claim, not a consequence of the two named assumptions above, and we flag it as such, since it is more plausible when persona construction and context assignment are themselves independent processes (true by design in §5.3’s experimental assignment; requires separate justification wherever context is observationally sampled rather than assigned).

Under this simplification,

I((πp,Xc);Δp,c∣λp,Dp)≤ϵ1+ϵ2=:ϵ.I\big((\pi_{p},X_{c});\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p}\big)\leq\epsilon_{1}+\epsilon_{2}=:\epsilon.

By Proposition 1, Rp,c𝒜=g⁡(πp,Xc)+ηp,cR^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c}=g(\pi_{p},X_{c})+\eta_{p,c} with gg a deterministic function of (πp,Xc)(\pi_{p},X_{c}) and ηp,c\eta_{p,c} independent of Δp,c\Delta_{p,c}; the data processing inequality then gives I(Rp,c𝒜;Δp,c∣λp,Dp)≤I((πp,Xc);Δp,c∣λp,Dp)≤ϵI(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c};\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p})\leq I\big((\pi_{p},X_{c});\Delta_{p,c}\mid\lambda_{p},D_{p}\big)\leq\epsilon. Applying Pinsker’s inequality and the same bounded-outcome argument as Corollary 1,

|Cov⁡(Rp,c𝒜,Δp,c)|≤4​M2​ϵ/2=4​M2​(ϵ1+ϵ2)/2.\left|\mathrm{Cov}(R^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,c},\Delta_{p,c})\right|\leq 4M^{2}\sqrt{\epsilon/2}=4M^{2}\sqrt{(\epsilon_{1}+\epsilon_{2})/2}.

As with the single-assumption case, this degrades gracefully rather than collapsing, since the bound scales with the combined violation of both assumptions, and remains small whenever both ϵ1\epsilon_{1} and ϵ2\epsilon_{2} are small, which is the expected case for closed-schema personas under experimentally assigned contexts, and the case requiring the most caution for rich, open-ended personas under observationally sampled ones.

B.5. Assumption defensibility across the fixed-persona family

Each assumption is more plausible for some designs than for others. The Key Assumption is strongest for closed-schema personas built from fixed demographic or categorical fields, which have no channel for person-specific cross-context deviation. It is weaker for rich, open-ended personas such as interview transcripts, which could incidentally encode traits correlated with person-specific activation. There Corollary 1 or Corollary 2 carries the argument in place of the exact-zero result, and the degradation is graceful (small ϵ1\epsilon_{1}, small bound). The Context Exogeneity Assumption is strongest for experimentally assigned contexts, such as the between-subject theme randomization in §5.3, and weaker for observationally sampled ones, such as the subreddit choices in §5.2, where a person’s tendencies could influence which contexts they appear in. Corollary 2 carries the argument there, and §4.3 states this as a scope condition.

Appendix C Identity-State Specifications and Empirical Methodology

This appendix collects the construction detail, calibration history, and supporting validation for the two empirical demonstrations in §5.2 and §5.3. None of this detail is needed to evaluate the paper’s central claims, which are stated in full in the main text. It is provided for reproducibility and for readers who want to check the specific engineering decisions behind Arm C in each domain. We call a specification locked when it was fixed in writing before the run it governs.

Table 3 summarizes both domains’ main results side by side, organized by arm rather than by domain, with the reading each result supports.

C.1. Full Chameleon Empirical Test

The target population is 1,667 Reddit users (Chameleon (Harry et al., 2026)), each with three posts across distinct subreddits, scored on five Big Five personality constructs plus twenty-one auxiliary trait dimensions using SEANCE, a psycholinguistic text-analysis tool that scores language for psychological content. The real signal is faint. Bias-corrected ICC(1) is approximately 0.01 to 0.02 across all five constructs, so 98 to 101% of real variance is within-person, with the upper end above 100% because Neuroticism’s bias-corrected estimate is slightly negative (−0.007-0.007, Table 4), a known property of this estimator when the true value is near zero. Real person-context interaction variance is small in absolute terms, at 0.072 for extraversion, 0.049 for agreeableness, 0.067 for conscientiousness, 0.022 for neuroticism, and 0.043 for openness.

Each user’s own three real (user, subreddit) cells are simulated under the three arms of §5.1. Arm A’s persona is a bio built from the user’s twenty-one non-Big-Five dimensions (Schwartz Values, Self-Determination Theory, and the DOSPERT risk-taking scale), and the Big Five is excluded because it is the outcome, so that the model cannot echo the answer. Arm B adds the subreddit name. Arm C adds the active identity state (Appendix C.2). The full-scale run covers all 1,667 users with two or three replicates per cell, in the hybrid reasoning-and-rating format of Appendix C.5.

Results.

ICC. Real ICC clusters in a narrow, near-zero band (0.01 to 0.02). Arms A and B invert this near-completely, with between-person shares of 83 to 95% for Arm A (mean 0.909) and 60 to 89% for Arm B (mean 0.799) against a real mean of 0.013, as §3.3 predicts. Arm C’s aggregate ICC (mean 0.285) sits substantially closer to the real value, but the improvement is not uniform (Table 4). Extraversion is recovered almost exactly, while agreeableness, conscientiousness, and openness overshoot by roughly 24 to 65-fold, and neuroticism overshoots more strongly in the negative direction. A person-in-context design that had recovered the real structure would show similarly small ICC on every construct, whereas Arm C’s values spread widely across constructs.

Person-specific signal. This is the direct test of Proposition 2, computed across approximately 4,568 person-context comparisons per construct (Table 5). The mean correlation is 0.026 for Arm A, 0.025 for Arm B, and 0.004 for Arm C, near zero for every arm. Arm A is significant on three of five constructs (extraversion, conscientiousness, neuroticism), Arm B on two, and Arm C on one (extraversion). Small positive values for the fixed-persona arms are what the robustness corollary expects. Arm C’s point estimates are negative on agreeableness and conscientiousness, but its intervals include zero, as do all arms’ intervals on openness. The detectability analysis below shows that the test cannot separate the arms at this size.

Detectability. Each person-specific correlation rests on about 4,570 person-context comparisons per construct, and its interval comes from a bootstrap that resamples whole users (1,000 resamples). The standard errors implied by those intervals are 0.012 to 0.016 (mean 0.0145), so an observed correlation must be about 0.033 to 0.045 (mean 0.041) to be detected with 80% power. A simulation that gives a synthetic system a known correlation with the real person-specific residuals confirms this, with detection rates of 78% at 0.04 and 98% at 0.05 (60 repetitions each). Arm A’s and Arm B’s mean correlations (0.026 and 0.025) lie below that size, and Arm C’s mean (0.004) lies far below it. The test therefore rules out an observed correlation well above 0.04 in every arm and cannot separate the arms below about 0.04. The real residual also contains post-level noise, so even a perfect simulator would score well below 1 on this measure, and a near-zero value does not show that person-specific signal is absent.

C.2. Identity-State Specification: Chameleon

Arm C’s set of identity states ℐp\mathcal{I}_{p} was built data-first. A six-component Gaussian mixture model was fit to the 1,667 users’ twenty-six-dimensional trait vectors (five Big Five constructs plus twenty-one auxiliary dimensions). Psychological interpretation of each component was applied only after fitting, through three independent blind literature-grounding panels that did not have access to each other’s labels until convergence was checked.

The panels converged on treating the largest, least-differentiated component (40.3% weight) as an unmarked statistical baseline rather than a distinct activated identity state, in the spirit of Fleeson’s view of a trait as the center of a distribution of states (§3.2). The state-typical shift term m⁡(λp,c)m(\lambda_{p},c) excludes this baseline component. The remaining five components, ranging from 2.7% to 21.4% weight, carry Arm C’s context-conditional behavior. Table 6 names and interprets all six. Figure 3 diagrams the full pipeline below, from the raw trait vectors through to how each arm is scored against real people.

Table 7 gives the wording that Arm C passes to the model for each activated state. The baseline component has no wording, since it is not an activated state.

Calibration history.

The initial construction used each user’s raw GMM posterior λp\lambda_{p} directly as the activation signal, which failed because posteriors are extreme by construction (95.9% of users have over 90% of their non-baseline mass on a single identity state), leaving context almost no room to compete with a person’s default identity state. Context-conditioned and static top-2 identity state selections were identical in 97.3% of piloted cells.

The fix separates affinity (which identity states are available to a person, drawn from λp\lambda_{p}) from activation (which identity state is realized in a specific context). This adopts the same weight-times-cue-match structure independently arrived at for the motivational-themes study’s identity state competition (below), in which a modest affinity weight wp,rw_{p,r} is combined with a context-only cue-match score ar,ca_{r,c}, and the realized activation is arg⁡maxr⁡wp,r⋅ar,c\arg\max_{r}\,w_{p,r}\cdot a_{r,c}.

C.3. Identity-State Specification: Motivational-Themes Study

Arm C’s set of identity states ℐp\mathcal{I}_{p} here was built literature-first, the inverse of Chameleon’s data-first approach. Six theory-grounded identity states were specified from the health-behavior and clinical-trial-recruitment literature, independent of the target study’s own findings. Two of the six identity states never activate for this study’s four stimuli specifically, by intended construction, since not every identity state in the set is relevant to every domain the set might be reused in. Figure 4 diagrams the full pipeline, including Medical Skeptic’s direct trust gate and how the remaining five identity states compete for activation.

Circularity check.

Because this specification could not rule out prior exposure to the target study’s findings, an independent circularity check was run before locking the taxonomy. Three isolated LLM sessions were each given only a neutral task description (build a literature-grounded identity state taxonomy for this population and context) with no access to this specification or the target study’s findings, and instructed to disregard the target study if it surfaced in their own search. One session had zero exposure to the study across its entire search. Their independently built taxonomies were compared against the draft specification for convergence, driving two merges, one addition (an identity state that emerged unprompted in all three), and giving Medical Skeptic, the identity state the paper’s reproduction target depends on, the strongest independent convergence of all six.

Medical Skeptic is the identity state the reproduction target theoretically depends on. It is driven primarily by trust tertile, with base activation rates of 0.70 for distrust, 0.35 for neutral, and 0.15 for trust, plus capped secondary demographic correlates that are constrained so they cannot outvote trust itself.

Table 8 gives the wording and the affinity rules for all six states. A person’s affinity for a state is 11 plus the sum of the bumps for the demographic categories they belong to. When the Medical Skeptic gate does not fire, the state with the highest affinity times cue score among the other five is active. Medical Skeptic’s activation probability is the trust base rate plus a constant 0.05 for the institutional framing present in every ad, plus 0.03 for each of three secondary correlates (rural residence, age 60 or older, a bachelor’s degree or higher), clipped to the range 0.05 to 0.95.

Table 9 gives the cue scores for the four ads, which are fixed numbers set in the code. The Medical Skeptic entry applies to the earlier shared competition (versions 1.1 to 1.3). Under the trust gate that replaced it, institutional framing adds a constant 0.05 to its activation probability for every ad.

Calibration history.

Arm C’s mechanism required four locked revisions before passing internal-validity checks, each triggered by a specific diagnostic failure rather than outcome-directed tuning. The first implementation, a literature-cited competition among all six identity states, was not self-calibrating, since individually well-grounded modifier magnitudes let the intended trait be outvoted by unrelated, more prevalent correlates (a college-education correlate common to 76% of the pilot personas overwhelmed the trust-distrust modifier defining Medical Skeptic). The mechanism that finally passed instead special-cases Medical Skeptic as a direct function of its own defining trait.

The theme-amplified refinement.

Locked before evaluation, this refinement amplifies the trust-linked identity state’s activation spread specifically for the blood-pressure theme. It is reported in the main text as a weaker test than the domain-general mechanism, since the amplified theme was chosen with knowledge of where the real effect is located. In both domains, literature or statistical grounding alone did not guarantee that a mechanism let context and person jointly determine behavior, so each mechanism was checked directly with the diagnostics above.

Model-based steps.

In Chameleon, the context cue-matching score ar,ca_{r,c} is produced by Claude Haiku 4.5, the same language model that generates persona behavior, in a separate call. This is an LLM-as-judge design in the sense of Zheng et al. (2023) and Gu et al. (2026). In the motivational-themes study the cue scores are fixed integers from 0 to 2 for each ad theme (Table 9), set in the code from the specification’s activation cues. The Medical Skeptic score was raised from 1 to 2 after the first pilot showed that the state never activated, and the state was later replaced by a direct trust gate. The literature-grounding and circularity-check panels described above and in Appendices C.2 and C.3 were isolated agent sessions of Claude Sonnet 5.5 run through Claude Code, with no access to each other’s output. They were not human raters. §6.4 discusses the resulting judge-and-subject concern.

C.4. Motivational-Themes Study: Analysis Specification and Robustness

Published target.

Table 10 lists the design and results of the study that serve as the target in §5.3.

What was compared.

The real study reports six blood-pressure by trust coefficients, one for each of three outcomes (appeal, willingness to participate, willingness to recommend) at each trust extreme, relative to neutral trust and to the contribution-to-science theme. For each simulated arm we estimate the same six interactions and record whether the sign matches the published sign. All six published coefficients are negative, so direction-uncorrelated guessing matches 3 of 6 on average. Table 12 lists the six simulated coefficients for each arm under the main-text specification.

Specification choice.

Before computing any arm’s results, we fixed one primary specification to mirror the original study, an ordered logit (a cumulative-link model) for each outcome, with theme and trust interacted, the contribution-to-science theme and neutral trust as baselines, and the demographic adjusters of the published model. The original model has a random intercept for repeated measures. We replace it with standard errors clustered by persona. The main text reports a linear version of the same model, which gives contrasts in rating points, for the following reason. Simulated ratings follow the trust tier almost deterministically. In Arm A’s appeal ratings the fitted trust effects reach +6.4+6.4 and −11.9-11.9 log-odds, which is close to separation, and the ordered-logit interaction coefficients are then unstable in size. A shift of −0.12-0.12 rating points appears as −1.7-1.7 log-odds. Sign counts are the same under both models for the baseline we use (Table 11), so this choice does not change the direction results. With 6,632 personas almost every coefficient is statistically significant, so we compare direction and size and give significance only for reference.

Within-person check.

Figure 5 shows the paired differences behind the natural-experiment result in §5.3.3.

Why Arm B matches none.

Table 13 shows the cause. In Arm B, the contribution-to-science theme at neutral trust has a mean appeal of 3.49, against 3.09 in Arm A. Every interaction is measured against that baseline cell, so its height sets the sign of all six coefficients. We report the pattern and have not tested why the theme sentence raises that cell.

C.5. Elicitation-Format Validation

Both empirical demonstrations use a hybrid {reasoning, rating} structured-output format, in which the model gives a short reasoning and then a rating. We chose it in a pilot on eight persona-context pairs from the motivational-themes study (20 samples each, Claude Haiku 4.5, temperature 0.7). The pairs were drawn from an earlier 20-pair pilot, five where a bare structured rating gave identical answers across all 20 samples and three where it did not. The pilot compared three formats, namely a bare structured rating, free text ending in a rating, and the hybrid. Table 14 gives the mean sampling variance of the appeal rating.

The bare format gave the lowest variance, and the hybrid recovered about 37% of the gap between the bare format and free text. With eight pairs the intervals overlap, so this is a pilot-scale result. Low variance in the model’s ratings would hide interaction effects whatever the activation mechanism does, so a format that does not suppress variance was a precondition for a fair test. We chose the hybrid over free text because its schema-validated output guarantees parseable responses at the scale of the main runs (about 25,000 responses for the motivational-themes study). Free text parsed at 100% in this 160-response test, but one small run with one prompt template does not guarantee that at scale.

Appendix D Example Personas, Prompts, and Run Metadata

This appendix shows what the language model receives in each arm, using the exact templates from our code. The example people are constructed with the same templates and are not real individuals. Wording that would identify the study’s authors or institution is replaced by a bracketed note.

D.1. Three Families, One Person and One Situation

Table 15 shows the same constructed person facing the same ad in each family. The memory-evolving row is an illustration of the family and was not evaluated in our experiments.

D.2. Motivational-Themes Study: Prompts by Arm

All arms share the opening of the system prompt: “You are simulating the survey response of a specific person for a research study on synthetic population simulation. Respond only as this person would. Do not break character or comment on the task.” It is followed by “Persona:” and the demographic line from Table 15.

  • •

    Arm A adds the trust sentence for the person’s tier. The three sentences are: “Based on your life experience, you generally distrust medical institutions and clinical research.” (distrust), “You have a fairly neutral, wait-and-see attitude toward medical institutions and clinical research.” (neutral), and “Based on your life experience, you generally trust medical institutions and clinical research.” (trust).

  • •

    Arm B adds the same trust sentence plus one sentence naming the ad theme: “This ad emphasizes contributing to scientific research.” (research), “This ad emphasizes improving the well-being of Black communities.” (community), “This ad emphasizes personal health benefit, specifically improving your own blood pressure.” (blood pressure), or “This ad emphasizes free groceries or cash compensation.” (perks).

  • •

    Arm C adds no trust sentence. It adds “Right now, this person’s salient concern is:” followed by the norm of the selected identity state. The six states are Community & Scientific Contribution, Health Focused, Medical Skeptic, Prudential Consumer, Privacy & Surveillance Wary, and Faith-Centered Providence, and their full wording is in Appendix C.3.

The user turn is identical in all arms and consists of the ad followed by the outcome question. The ad has the form “[study name]; [theme headline]; A 12-week research study investigating the potential impact of fresh groceries on lowering blood pressure in Black adults. [contact line removed for review]”. The four headlines are “Join our clinical trial to advance scientific research!”, “Join our clinical trial to study a way to improve the well-being of Black communities!”, “Join our clinical trial to study a dietary approach to improve your blood pressure!”, and “Join our clinical trial to receive either free delivered fresh groceries or cash!” The outcome question reads: “Assume [the medical center] is a research hospital near where you live. Please review the clinical trial advertisement above and rate how much you agree or disagree with the following statements, each on a 5-point scale (5 = Strongly agree, 4 = Somewhat agree, 3 = Neither agree or disagree, 2 = Somewhat disagree, 1 = Strongly disagree): (1) appeal – ‘This clinical trial recruitment advertisement is appealing to me’; (2) participate – ‘I plan to call or email [the medical center] to participate in this clinical trial’; (3) recommend – ‘I plan to share this clinical trial advertisement with others who may be eligible’. Give a brief reasoning, then the three ratings.” The model returns a short reasoning and three integer ratings from 1 to 5 as structured output.

D.3. Chameleon: Prompts by Arm

The persona line is built from the user’s trait scores. We rank 21 trait dimensions (values, motivation, and risk attitudes) by how far they are from average, keep the five largest, and write one sentence for each in the high or low form. The five Big Five constructs are the outcome and are never in the persona. An example for a constructed user, whose top five traits include novelty-seeking and comfort with social risk, is: “Persona: This person seeks novelty, excitement, and new experiences. This person is comfortable with social risks, like disagreeing publicly. This person isn’t especially attached to tradition or custom. This person doesn’t feel especially connected to other people right now. This person sticks closely to ethical rules.”

All arms share the opening: “You are simulating how a specific person would come across in a piece of short writing, for a research study on synthetic population simulation. Respond only as this person would. Do not break character or comment on the task.” The user turn ends with the same rating question in every arm: “Rate how much each of the following describes how you’re coming across right now, on a 1-5 scale (1 = not at all, 5 = very much): extraversion (outgoing, energetic), agreeableness (warm, cooperative), conscientiousness (organized, disciplined), neuroticism (anxious, emotionally reactive), openness (curious, open to new ideas). Give a brief reasoning, then the five ratings.”

  • •

    Arm A: the user turn begins “You are about to write a short post online.”

  • •

    Arm B: the same persona, and the user turn begins “You are about to write a short post in the r/[subreddit] community on Reddit.”

  • •

    Arm C: the same user turn as Arm B, and the system prompt adds “Right now, the aspect of this person’s identity that’s most active is:” followed by up to two identity states from Appendix C.2, for example “Primarily Expansive Engaged (socially confident and broadly engaged across many areas of life, comfortable taking risks in multiple domains).”

For Arm C, a separate call scores each subreddit once against the five activation cues. The system prompt reads “You are scoring how well a Reddit community’s typical content matches a set of behavioral/content cues, for a research study on context-activated identity. Score based on the community’s general content and tone, not any specific post.” The user turn reads “Community: r/[subreddit]. For each set of cues below, score 0, 1, or 2 how well r/[subreddit]’s typical content matches it (0 = no match, 1 = some/background match, 2 = strong/central match)”, followed by the five cue descriptions, and the model returns a short reasoning and one score per state. The cue descriptions are, in the order of Table 7:

  • •

    Expansive Engaged. Content involving active social engagement, competitive or achievement framing, novelty-seeking, or discussion of risk-taking across financial, recreational, or social domains, such as competitive gaming, entrepreneurship and investing, adventure or physical-risk activities, active dating, and high-energy outgoing social interaction.

  • •

    Amotivated Disinhibited. Content reflecting disengagement, low investment, or venting without goal-orientation, combined with casual mentions of rule-bending, safety-cutting-corners, or gambling, such as low-effort complaining, confession-style rule-breaking, casual gambling or lottery discussion, and anonymous low-investment participation.

  • •

    High-Intensity Reactive. Content involving high emotional intensity combined with high personal investment or striving, but not framed around risk-taking, such as high-stakes personal-crisis discussion, competitive achievement under pressure, and emotionally charged advice-seeking where the poster is highly engaged and anxious.

  • •

    Quiet Withdrawn. Content that is low-stakes, passive, or solitary, such as casual browsing or lurker-friendly communities, simple hobby or leisure content without competitive or social-striving framing, and low posting or interaction demands.

  • •

    Conventional Risk-Tolerant. Content that frames risk-taking within a conventional or practical, duty-oriented lens, such as personal finance or insurance framed around family responsibility, traditional-values-adjacent communities where practical rule-bending is normalized, and health or safety trade-offs made for practical or family reasons.
